action: Buy Hong Kong Disneyland tickets only through official resort channels or authorised travel agents; do not buy from unofficial resellers, as stolen codes may circulate.
date_note: Resort announced the incident on Friday 13 Nov; staff found unusual activity on the evening of 12 Nov.
exec: A major tourist venue paused online sales after ticket codes were reportedly stolen, showing ticketing systems are direct targets.
plain: Hong Kong Disneyland found a cyber incident in its online ticketing system and stopped selling tickets and hotel rooms online. About 17,000 ticket QR codes were reported stolen. Police are investigating.
summary: Hong Kong Disneyland said it recently detected a cybersecurity incident, suspended online ticket and hotel sales, reported it to police and tightened gate checks. The Standard reports about 17,000 e-ticket QR codes were stolen; the resort did not itself verify that number. Police classed it as accessing a computer with criminal or dishonest intent; no arrests. The resort plans to notify the privacy commissioner.
title: Hong Kong Disneyland suspends online sales after about 17,000 ticket QR codes reported stolen

validation.note: The Standard and eSecurity Planet (citing SCMP); resort statement relayed; code count not independently verified by the resort.

review.note: Compared 12-13 Nov dates, about 17,000 QR codes unverified by resort, police classification, no arrests, PCPD, suspension against The Standard and eSecurity Planet
